# dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator
**See the current DeepSeek API pricing window at a glance in the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI.**
A single 5px dot sits in the composer tool row, **just left of the model name** (**rendered only whe

n the
session's selected model provider is DeepSeek**):
| Color | Window | Price |

| 🟡 Yellow `#f2b705` | Peak hours | Standard |
| 🟢 Green `#22c55e` | Off-peak hours | Half price |

Nothing else is rendered — no text, no icon, no placeholder copy (the dot carries an
`aria-label` fo

r screen readers). No build step, no third-party dependencies: the whole
plugin is one file.
English | 中文
## When it shows

The dot renders only while the session's selected model provider is DeepSeek; otherwise it
renders n
othing at all and takes no space:
| Provider | Shows |

| `deepseek-official` (DeepSeek API key) | ✅ |
| `deepseek-account` (DeepSeek account) | ✅ |
| Anyth

ing else (Anthropic, an OpenAI-compatible gateway, a self-hosted proxy, …) | ❌ hidden |
| Unknown (m
odel directory still loading) | ❌ hidden |

The provider is what counts, not the model name — a third-party gateway serving a DeepSeek
model doe

s not get DeepSeek's time-of-day pricing. The rule lives in `isDeepSeekProvider()`;
change that one
function to change the policy.

The session's model directory is resolved **after mount, with retries**: a freshly switched
session

has not registered its scope yet, so the lookup legitimately fails for a moment. The
dot therefore a

ppears a fraction of a second after a session switch instead of staying hidden
for the whole session

pears a fraction of a second after a session switch instead of staying hidden
for the whole session.
## How the window is decided

Per DeepSeek's official pricing page
(Models & Pricing):

- **Peak**: Beijing time **Monday–Friday** (excluding Chinese statutory holidays),
**09:00–12:00** a

nd **14:00–18:00**;
- **Off-peak**: everything else, **including weekends and statutory holidays all

day**
(off-peak = half of the peak price).

Intervals are half-open: 12:00 and 18:00 sharp already count as off-peak, while 09:00 and
14:00 shar

p count as peak. All comparisons use `Asia/Shanghai`, so the machine's own time
zone does not matter

count as peak. All comparisons use `Asia/Shanghai`, so the machine's own time
zone does not matter.

> **Make-up workdays.** The official wording is "Monday to Friday … all other periods,
> including w

eekends and Chinese statutory holidays, are off-peak all day". A Saturday or
> Sunday that the gover

nment designates as a make-up workday therefore stays off-peak
> (green) here. Change the `WORKDAYS`
check in `client.js` if you disagree.

## Compatibility

Developed and verified on **macOS with DSH desktop 0.2.0-rc.2** (`install_bundle` returned
`applicat

ion: applied`; the `conversation.input.right` occupant reports `active: true`).
The plugin only uses

slot registration and React, so it should work on the same DSH
generation; a change to slot names o

r the `dsh.client` manifest contract would require an
update here.
